s12.title: Shaping the table
s12.lead: We found a table where one cell holds several values, or where a whole kind of value is itself a column's value. Choose which tables to use.

tabKind.pivot: Split into one table per kind of value — {{column}}
tabKind.flatten: Turn nested values into a table — {{column}}
tabKind.unnest: Turn a list into one row per value — {{column}}

s12.pivotIntro: We grouped spelling variants of the same kind of value. The tables you'll use are checked.
s12.colOtherUnits: Rows written with a different unit
s12.groupZeroRows: No rows matched the horizontal-axis value’s spelling, so applying this would give 0 rows (a spelling variant on that axis may be the cause).
s12.adoptOtherUnit: Treat as the same unit ({{unit}} · {{rows}} rows)
s12.adoptOtherUnitTitle: Add {{label}} ({{unit}}) to this table, treating it as the same unit
s12.mergedAwayTitle: Already merged into another table — cannot switch back to use
s12.partnerLabel: Value used as the horizontal axis: {{label}} ({{unit}})
s12.carryTitle: Columns to carry along as well
s12.carryNote: Choose columns from the original table you also want kept here (already-selected columns are highlighted).
s12.explodeIntro: The {{columns}} column(s) of this table hold several values in one cell. We'll open them into a table with one point per row.
s12.flattenIntro: The {{column}} column of this table has items nested inside each value. We'll make two tables: one long table with every item, and one wide table with the common items as columns.
s12.longNote: The long, one-item-per-row table keeps every item as it is (unchecking below does not remove it there).
s12.wideKeysNote: Checked items become columns in the one-row-per-record table.
s12.wideKeysNoteRate: The percentage is the share of source rows where that item has a value. Items differ by field, so you can also pick the rarer ones.
s12.wideFieldsTitle: What to put in the columns
s12.wideFieldsNote: Each item gets one column per checked part (at least one stays).
s12.samplesLost: The reload lost the file contents, so real-data examples could not be re-read. Please start over with "Choose different files".
s12.unnestIntroObject: In this table, the {{column}} column holds several values (a list) in one cell, and each value has its own items. We make a long table with one value per row, and keep the original order in a "which one" column.
s12.unnestIntroScalar: In this table, the {{column}} column holds several values (a list) in one cell. We make a long table with one value per row, and keep the original order in a "which one" column.
s12.unnestFieldsNote: Checked items become columns. Unchecked items are not lost: they stay together in one column, as JSON.
s12.unnestFieldsNoteRate: The percentage is the share of values in the list that have a value for that item.
s12.unnestNotList: {{count}} cells could not be read as a list (they stay as they are in the original table).
s12.unnestEmptyElements: {{count}} empty values were not turned into rows.

redesign.bannerNote: Nothing runs on its own here, and nothing has to be changed — if it all looks right, you can leave it as it is. Item meanings and units are rewritten as soon as you save them, without rebuilding the data (the item names on the pages that published IDs open change when you press “Update the published item names” on Try it). Changing how kinds are split, how they link, or how IDs are made rebuilds the draft, and Try it → Publish then publishes a new version.
redesign.structuralNote: This opens the screen with every setting. “Back to simple mode” brings you back here.
redesign.cancelConfirm: Stop reviewing and go back to the dataset page? (Changes already applied by the AI are saved.)
redesign.trialFailed: The trial queries could not run. Wait a moment and press "Try again", or finish reviewing as is.
redesign.findingsBody: Asking the AI to fix this rebuilds the draft; you can check the result in “try it → publish”. If you only want to adjust item meanings, you can dismiss this.

meanings.askConsultPrefill: Please fill in the meanings that are still blank

links.title: Pick the links
links.step1Title: ① Which number names this one item?
links.keyLead: Something that can always name the same one item later, by the same number: a serial number, model number, catalogue number. Measured values can't be picked.
links.keyQuestion: Which number names this one item?
links.keyMissing: No naming number has been picked yet. Choose one from the candidates above.
links.step2Title: ② Which values are links to other data?
links.lead: Which values also appear, spelled the same way, in other files or other people’s data? Tick the COLUMN those values live in and equal values connect automatically (in the carrot example, the ☑ goes on the “ingredient” column).
links.exampleCaption: Tick the ingredient name and the two tables connect on ingest — "recipes using carrot, and its current price" becomes one query.
links.whenYes: Tick — words and numbers that appear elsewhere with the same spelling: names of substances, products or places, fixed notations such as chemical formulas, official numbers such as DOIs or catalogue numbers.
links.whenNo: Do not tick — serial numbers that exist only inside this file, free-text notes. Ticking a measured number has no effect (it is dropped automatically).
links.whenSafe: Ticking never removes the item (it becomes a reference). You can change your picks any time before publishing.
links.askConsultPrefill: Which values for this one item are likely to appear in other data with the same spelling (values worth giving an ID)? Look at the columns and real values.
links.baseTitle: Match IDs to this data's own IRIs
links.baseLead: This column holds full IRIs (IDs starting with https://). Using their shared prefix as the ID base makes each row's ID here identical to the original IRI, so references handed out elsewhere connect as they are. Changing it after publishing means moving IDs, so this can only be decided during the first design.
links.baseUse: Use the prefix {{base}} of “{{column}}” as the ID base
links.baseRejected: The IRIs in “{{column}}” could not be used as the ID base for {{source}} ({{reason}}). Reverted to the IDs Asterism makes.

baseReason.not_iri_column: this column is not full IRIs
